# Maryland OHEP award history (MEAP & EUSP)

July–December timeline of **applications**, **households receiving benefits**, **average award**, and **total benefits paid** for Maryland OHEP bill-assistance grants — **MEAP** (heating) and **EUSP** (electric) — plus **PSC full-year EUSP** outcomes (FY2021–2024) and the **FY26 scheduled matrices** currently applied in rate-design-platform's Maryland LMI workflow.

**DLS data rule:** each program year is taken from the **most recent** DLS N00I0006 report that covers it (see `context/sources/md_hp_rates/ohep/DLS-OHEP-award-and-participation-history.md`):

| Values for FY | DLS report | Exhibit |
| ------------- | ---------- | ------- |
| 2021 | 2023FY | Ex. 2 (Jul–**Nov**) |
| 2022 | 2024FY | Ex. 2 (Jul–Dec) |
| 2023 | 2025FY | Ex. 10 (Jul–Dec) |
| 2024 | 2026FY | Ex. 9 (Jul–Dec) |
| 2025 & 2026 | 2027FY | Ex. 14 (Jul–Dec) |

These are **first-half (YTD)** snapshots, not full fiscal-year totals. FY 2025 Jul–Dec averages omit year-end supplemental grants (2027FY note).

```{python}

def timeline_gt(df: pl.DataFrame, program: str) -> None:
    gt = (
        GT(df, rowname_col="fy")
        .cols_label(
            applications="Applications",
            receiving_benefits="Receiving benefits",
            avg_benefit="Average benefit",
            benefits_paid_m="Benefits paid ($M)",
            source="Source exhibit",
        )
        .fmt_number(columns=["applications", "receiving_benefits"], decimals=0, use_seps=True)
        .fmt_currency(columns="avg_benefit", decimals=0)
        .fmt_number(columns="benefits_paid_m", decimals=1)
        .tab_stubhead(label=program)
        .tab_source_note(
            "*FY2021 window is July–November (2023FY Exhibit 2), not July–December. "
            "FY2025 Jul–Dec averages exclude year-end supplemental benefits."
        )
        .tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options())
    )
    display_gt(gt)


def meap_matrix_gt(df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:

            electric="Electric",

            oil_kerosene="Oil / kerosene",
            propane="Propane",
            wood_coal="Wood / coal",

        .fmt_currency(

        )
        .tab_stubhead(label="Poverty level")
        .tab_header(title="FY26 MEAP annual grant matrix (USD / program year)")
```

## DLS mid-year history

### MEAP (heating assistance)

```{python}
#| label: tbl-meap-history
#| tbl-cap: "MEAP applications, recipients, average benefit, and benefits paid (DLS Jul–Dec YTD)"
timeline_gt(meap_history, "MEAP")
```

Mid-year MEAP awards ran ~`$510` → peak ~`$849` (FY23) → still high in FY24 (`$761`) → collapse to **`$186`** in FY25 H1 → partial rebound to **`$290`** in FY26 H1. Households receiving benefits rose steadily (~40k → ~80k in the H1 window). Total benefits paid peaked mid-period (~`$43M` in FY24 H1) then fell with the FY25 cut.

### EUSP (electric bill assistance)

```{python}
#| label: tbl-eusp-history
#| tbl-cap: "EUSP bill payment applications, recipients, average benefit, and benefits paid (DLS Jul–Dec YTD)"
timeline_gt(eusp_history, "EUSP bill payment")
```

Mid-year EUSP average awards peaked at **`$939`** (FY23), fell to **`$668`** (FY24) and **`$252`** (FY25 H1), then recovered to **`$518`** (FY26 H1). Receiving-benefits counts and applications both stepped up sharply after categorical eligibility (FY24 onward). Benefits paid in the H1 window: ~`$19M` → peak **`$44.9M`** (FY23) → **`$18M`** (FY25) → **`$42M`** (FY26).

### EUSP full-year outcomes (PSC, FY2021–2024)

Closed fiscal-year EUSP **bill payment** results from the PSC statutory annual reports. These are full-year unique households and spend — so **households served** run about **~2×** the DLS Jul–Dec “Receiving Benefits” counts above (same program, different window).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-eusp-full-year
#| tbl-cap: "PSC full-year EUSP bill assistance: households served, total expense, and average grant (FY2021–2024)"
eusp_full_year_gt(eusp_full_year)
```

Full-year average grants: **`$504`** → **`$763`** → peak **`$939`** (FY23) → **`$628`** (FY24). Households served rose from ~80–84k (FY21–22) to **114,230** in FY24 after categorical eligibility. Total bill-assistance spend peaked at **`$90.4M`** in FY23, then **`$71.6M`** in FY24.

## FY26 award matrices used in the MD LMI workflow

rate-design-platform applies these **scheduled annual grants** via `utils/post/apply_md_ohep_to_master_bills.py`, reading `utils/post/data/md_ohep_benefits.yaml` (`program_year: fy26`). Only poverty levels **1–5** are modeled; levels 6 (subsidized/sub-metered) and 7 (categorical >200% FPL) are excluded. Annual grants are allocated across months in the master-bills post-process.

Companion extracts: `context/sources/md_hp_rates/ohep/FY26-MEAP-Benefit-Matrix.md`, `FY26-EUSP-Benefit-Matrix.md`.

### MEAP matrix (by poverty level × heating fuel)

```{python}
#| label: tbl-meap-matrix
#| tbl-cap: "FY26 MEAP annual grant amounts currently applied in the Maryland LMI workflow"
meap_matrix_gt(meap_matrix)
```

Electric-heat MEAP awards are flat at **`$100`**/year across levels 1–5. Gas/wood awards run **`$300`–`$550`**; oil **`$650`–`$1,100`**; propane **`$600`–`$1,000`**.

### EUSP matrix (by poverty level × heating fuel × annual kWh)

Gas, oil/kerosene, propane, and wood/coal share the same FY26 EUSP band amounts, so the non-electric table below covers all four fuels.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-eusp-matrix-electric
#| tbl-cap: "FY26 EUSP annual grants for electric-heat customers (by poverty level and kWh band)"
eusp_matrix_gt(eusp_matrix_electric, "electric heat")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-eusp-matrix-non-electric
#| tbl-cap: "FY26 EUSP annual grants for non-electric heat (gas / oil / propane / wood; identical bands)"
eusp_matrix_gt(eusp_matrix_non_electric, "non-electric heat")
```

Electric-heat EUSP grants run **`$650`–`$1,000`**; non-electric heat **`$175`–`$500`**, rising with poverty severity and annual kWh band.

## Statewide participation (~48%)

rate-design-platform models OHEP take-up at **~48%** of eligible households: FY2025 full-year unique recipients ≈ **130k** (MEAP 128,926 / EUSP 130,046; dual receipt is the norm) ÷ DHS’s FY2025 planning eligible count of **270,000**. Sources and caveats: `context/sources/md_hp_rates/ohep/DHS-MFR-and-DLS-overall-participation-rates.md`; derivation also in RDP `context/domain/charges/lmi_discounts_in_md.md`.

That **48% does not line up with the older ~25–27%** by-program overall rates (APPRISE FY2017; DLS through FY2020). Those used a much larger ACS/APPRISE eligible pool (~**380k**). The same ~130k recipients on that pool would be ~**34%**, not 48%. So the jump is mostly **denominator**, not a sudden doubling of enrollment. Treat 48% as DHS **planning** take-up for FY25, not as a 1:1 update of the historical APPRISE/DLS series.

## Bottom line for modeling

We apply the **FY26 scheduled matrices** above (not the DLS mid-year realized averages). On the Jul–Dec DLS series, FY26 average awards (`$290` MEAP / `$518` EUSP) are a **partial recovery** from the FY25 trough, still below the FY22–FY23 peak — especially MEAP, which remains well under FY21–FY24 mid-year averages. FY26 is representative of the current post-categorical-eligibility regime, not of a simple five-year mean of these H1 averages. Participation for the production LMI scenario remains **`--lmi-participation-rates … 0.48`**, with the eligible-pool caveat above.
